quotes.text:
The promise of AI is real. But I want to be clear: our job here is not to applaud the promise.

It is to make sure AI is being used responsibly, safely, and transparently.

AI is going to be a critical tool to help deliver health care to veterans in the 21st century. We must take the necessary steps to ensure we use it wisely and that we’re protecting our veterans' data and information. Thank you to @michiganstateu’s Dr. Mohammad Ghassemi for joining my @HouseVetAffairs Technology Modernization Subcommittee hearing today to discuss how AI can improve health care for veterans.

I think that anything that presents a threat to national security or threats to human life ought to be given the full weight of attention necessary to deal with those. And Congress has a role to play in this.

So if we simply vacate altogether or ban AI entirely, which is not a feasible option, then we would be ceding that over to adversaries of ours that don't have our best interests in mind, certainly don't have the morals and ethics of guardrails that the United States would hope to achieve, and could certainly be used in a way that would subordinate the United States and our interests if we allow that to happen.

Uh, so my bill would prohibit the development and the use of fully autonomous weapons on the battlefield. I think that there has to be a human decision maker when we're dealing with things like lethal force, things like that on the uh on the battlefield in an offensive way.

Artificial intelligence is playing an increasingly critical role in strengthening our national defense, but it should never be the one making life-or-death decisions. We must establish safeguards now to ensure these technologies are used ethically and transparently. This bipartisan bill sets clear limits to make sure people stay in control whenever lethal force is involved while allowing our military to continue leading the world in technological innovation.

Life-and-death decisions should never be outsourced to artificial intelligence. That’s why I introduced bipartisan legislation last week to put clear safeguards in place for autonomous tech in our military to make sure a human — not a computer — is in control of lethal force.
https://t.co/NMIYWu5u9M

Health insurance companies should never rely on AI to decide if a treatment is medically necessary. That’s why this week, @RepGregLandsman and I introduced the bipartisan Doctors Not AI Act to make sure doctors are the ones deciding what care you and your family need. https://t.co/14kShHALyZ

AI is transforming the world we live in unlike anything we’ve seen before. It’s clear we need an international agreement to put strong guardrails on this rapidly developing technology before it’s too late.

Today, I called on @SecRubio and @USAmbUN to work with other nations to begin that process and address the current and future risks of AI.

I introduced the No Secrets for Data Centers Act because officials at every level of government shouldn’t be able to hide behind NDAs when it comes to data center development. 

Residents need to have a clear understanding of what Big Tech companies and data center developers are doing in their communities. 

I’m fighting every single day to give mid-Michigan a voice against AI and Big Tech.

The 81st Session of the UN General Assembly is uniquely positioned to begin these conversations with other countries. This should not only happen with our allies, but our adversaries as well. While we may have disagreements, we should all work towards the common goal of ensuring this technology is properly regulated for the common good and safety of all countries.

This next frontier in emerging technology has the ability to propel this world into a golden age or send us into collapse. I respectfully request that you both work to create regular and consistent multilateral dialogue on AI moving forward. It is critical that we begin these talks before it is too late.

AI has the potential to advance our society in ways we never thought possible, but it doesn’t come without risk. That’s why I’m fighting to put safeguards around this innovative technology and urging the Trump administration to negotiate an AI treaty that keeps our world safe.
https://t.co/bfp26sPQg7

Will claims to not take any corporate PAC money. 

But he begged the DCCC (which takes millions in corporate PAC money) to bankroll his campaign and guess what: they are.

The DCCC is funneling hundreds of thousands of dollars from Big Pharma, AI companies, and Data Center Developers right into Will’s pocket. He won’t give the money back because he’s that desperate for power.

Learn more about this legislation to ensure a comprehensive AI policy with serious guardrails:
https://t.co/aEGFCK9kF3

The rapid development of AI, which has potential to improve our society, has also exposed serious dangers. These risks cannot be ignored, and my new bill will create a seat at the Cabinet table for an official to monitor AI technology, ensure strong guardrails, and prepare us for this new era of technological innovation and beyond.

We are already seeing [AI] replace American jobs, threaten our national security, and degrade human dignity. [...] These risks cannot be ignored, so it's time to create a seat at the table for someone to monitor AI technology, ensure strong guardrails are in place, and prepare us for this new era of technological innovation and beyond.

The United States government has a fundamental responsibility to protect its citizens from all threats, including those we might not see coming. The rapid development of AI technology, which has potential to improve our society, has exposed the serious dangers that can come with it.
